question.question: When an applied implicit-joint configuration requests automatic exit, can leadership transfer reject the last application-triggered leave proposal and then time out while the same leader remains healthy, with no implementation-owned continuation to propose exit in an otherwise idle cluster?
question.importance: A lost configuration-completion continuation can retain outgoing voters and joint quorum requirements after removal/replacement was requested, obstructing subsequent configuration changes and reducing availability. This is a scoped progress concern; no consensus-safety violation is presumed.
contexts: Same retained leader term after a bounded failed leadership transfer
Configuration genuinely committed and applied before acknowledgment
Reliable ongoing heartbeat/Ready processing after bounded transport loss, no unrelated client proposal
event_paths: ProposeConfChange -> commit -> Ready.CommittedEntries -> ApplyConfChange -> transfer begins -> Advance -> appliedTo -> MsgProp rejected
Tick -> transfer timeout -> abortLeaderTransfer -> heartbeat-only Ready/Advance

supporting_behavior_ids.B-transfer: Produces and removes the proposal blocker without itself creating application work.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-application: Determines whether Ready/Advance actually produces the next appliedTo trigger.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-formation: Commits joint entry under actual voter quorums; a later unrelated proposal is a possible rescue, not yet an established caller duty.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-authority: Successful transfer or later election provides an alternative leader/no-op/application path.

counterevidence: appliedTo retries on later applied entries; a successful transfer/new leader can append and apply a no-op.
Transfer timeout is bounded by electionTimeout and ordinary proposals are admitted after abort.

Existing TestRawNodeJointAutoLeave expects recovery after leadership loss and reelection, but does not test failed transfer with the same idle leader; parts of that test explicitly pretend a config applied, so it is not a legal-history driver to reuse unexamined.
Caller proposals may be dropped, and their retries are external. Need distinguish that from the documented AutoLeave continuation once the entering configuration was already committed/applied.
unknowns: Construct a legal Ready/application history that overlaps transfer with the final application acknowledgment without excluding the relevant overlap or fabricating peer support.
Determine whether periodic ticks, real message delivery and empty Ready/Advance cycles generate a later application trigger after all entering-config work drains.
Ground any progress oracle in automatic proposal continuation, not an invented numeric deadline; a finite no-exit window alone cannot establish infinite stalling.
question.trigger_rationale: The explicit comment at appliedTo promises retry on next advance after failed transfer, but acceptReady queues an apply response only for nonempty committed entries and abortLeaderTransfer only clears its field. Contract/source reading supplies a concrete discriminator. A controlled real-node schedule can distinguish hidden continuation from reliance on later unrelated application. This is more informative than rerunning the explained obsolete-storage-response term guard; the configuration-commit/read-release lead needs more legal-history source work before execution.

materials.text:
Now that you are holding onto a Node you have a few responsibilities:

First, you must read from the Node.Ready() channel and process the updates
it contains. These steps may be performed in parallel, except as noted in step
2.

1. Write HardState, Entries, and Snapshot to persistent storage if they are
not empty. Note that when writing an Entry with Index i, any
previously-persisted entries with Index >= i must be discarded.

2. Send all Messages to the nodes named in the To field. It is important that
no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk,
and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while
entries from the same batch are being persisted). To reduce the I/O latency, an
optimization can be applied to make leader write to disk in parallel with its
followers (as explained at section 10.2.1 in Raft thesis). If any Message has type
MsgSnap, call Node.ReportSnapshot() after it has been sent (these messages may be
large).

Note: Marshalling messages is not thread-safe; it is important that you
make sure that no new entries are persisted while marshalling.
The easiest way to achieve this is to serialize the messages directly inside
your main raft loop.

3. Apply Snapshot (if any) and CommittedEntries to the state machine.
If any committed Entry has Type EntryConfChange, call Node.ApplyConfChange()
to apply it to the node. The configuration change may be cancelled at this point
by setting the NodeID field to zero before calling ApplyConfChange
(but ApplyConfChange must be called one way or the other, and the decision to cancel
must be based solely on the state machine and not external information such as
the observed health of the node).

4. Call Node.Advance() to signal readiness for the next batch of updates.
This may be done at any time after step 1, although all updates must be processed
in the order they were returned by Ready.

Second, all persisted log entries must be made available via an
implementation of the Storage interface. The provided MemoryStorage
type can be used for this (if you repopulate its state upon a
restart), or you can supply your own disk-backed implementation.

Third, when you receive a message from another node, pass it to Node.Step:

	func recvRaftRPC(ctx context.Context, m raftpb.Message) {
		n.Step(ctx, m)
	}

Finally, you need to call Node.Tick() at regular intervals (probably
via a time.Ticker). Raft has two important timeouts: heartbeat and the
election timeout. However, internally to the raft package time is
represented by an abstract "tick".

# Raft library

Raft is a protocol with which a cluster of nodes can maintain a replicated state machine.
The state machine is kept in sync through the use of a replicated log.
For more details on Raft, see "In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm"
(https://raft.github.io/raft.pdf) by Diego Ongaro and John Ousterhout.

This Raft library is stable and feature complete. As of 2016, it is **the most widely used** Raft library in production, serving tens of thousands clusters each day. It powers distributed systems such as etcd, Kubernetes, Docker Swarm, Cloud Foundry Diego, CockroachDB, TiDB, Project Calico, Flannel, Hyperledger and more.

Most Raft implementations have a monolithic design, including storage handling, messaging serialization, and network transport. This library instead follows a minimalistic design philosophy by only implementing the core raft algorithm. This minimalism buys flexibility, determinism, and performance.

To keep the codebase small as well as provide flexibility, the library only implements the Raft algorithm; both network and disk IO are left to the user. Library users must implement their own transportation layer for message passing between Raft peers over the wire. Similarly, users must implement their own storage layer to persist the Raft log and state.

In order to easily test the Raft library, its behavior should be deterministic. To achieve this determinism, the library models Raft as a state machine.  The state machine takes a `Message` as input. A message can either be a local timer update or a network message sent from a remote peer. The state machine's output is a 3-tuple `{[]Messages, []LogEntries, NextState}` consisting of an array of `Messages`, `log entries`, and `Raft state changes`. For state machines with the same state, the same state machine input should always generate the same state machine output.

A simple example application, _raftexample_, is also available to help illustrate how to use this package in practice: https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/tree/main/contrib/raftexample

# Features

This raft implementation is a full feature implementation of Raft protocol. Features includes:

- Leader election
- Log replication
- Log compaction
- Membership changes
- Leadership transfer extension
- Efficient linearizable read-only queries served by both the leader and followers
  - leader checks with quorum and bypasses Raft log before processing read-only queries
  - followers asks leader to get a safe read index before processing read-only queries
- More efficient lease-based linearizable read-only queries served by both the leader and followers
  - leader bypasses Raft log and processing read-only queries locally
  - followers asks leader to get a safe read index before processing read-only queries
  - this approach relies on the clock of the all the machines in raft group

This raft implementation also includes a few optional enhancements:

- Optimistic pipelining to reduce log replication latency
- Flow control for log replication
- Batching Raft messages to reduce synchronized network I/O calls
- Batching log entries to reduce disk synchronized I/O
- Writing to leader's disk in parallel
- Internal proposal redirection from followers to leader

after.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement
after.realization_summary: Leader appends qualified proposals, counts durable append support from configured voters under current-term commit validation, and propagates committed prefixes; followers preserve committed history and reject incompatible prefixes.

after.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority
after.realization_summary: Tick/Campaign, vote quorum and term dispatch acquire or relinquish local leadership. Reset invalidates transient support; transfer suppresses proposals until takeover or timeout while established committed state survives.

after.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation
after.realization_summary: Restart and snapshot handling rebuild history and participant configuration; replication probes, rejection hints and snapshots let lagging peers rejoin.
Committed configuration application changes voters and learner roles through simple/joint validation; AutoLeave is an implementation-owned proposal continuation triggered by acknowledged application.

Ready selects committed work with size/stability/snapshot bounds; caller application and Advance or local-worker response update applied accounting. Actual business state execution is outside this library.

after.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support
after.realization_summary: Storage and unstable overlay reconstruct log history; Ready separates durability-sensitive replies from immediate messages. In-repository MemoryStorage supplies a volatile backend; disk IO and durable writes are external caller duties.

after.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion
after.realization_summary: Node/RawNode exposes submission, read-index and completion APIs. Submission may be lost; caller retry/correlation and application through read index are needed for endpoint semantics.

after.execution_owner: RawNode Ready/Advance and caller application; Node serializes API calls
after.protocol_context: Committed, applying and applied positions in one raft instance
after.trigger: Ready selects committed work; caller finishes entries/snapshot; Advance or MsgStorageApplyResp acknowledges
legal_preconditions: Apply committed entries in order and call ApplyConfChange for accepted configuration entries; snapshots preserve returned ConfState.

Normal Advance normally follows application; Node interface permits early Advance while applying, but next Ready application cannot overtake previous work. Async responses follow actual worker completion.
implementation_guards: Do not return committed entries during pending/in-progress snapshot; limit outstanding application bytes.
Async application cannot pass unstable.offset-1; normal mode relies on the Ready caller persistence contract.
writes: Ready acceptance advances applying and charges bytes; completion advances applied monotonically and releases byte capacity.
important_branches: A nonempty committed-entry batch creates MsgStorageApplyResp; an empty heartbeat-only Ready does not.
Completion calls raft.appliedTo, which conditionally attempts automatic leave; this is not an unconditional effect of every Advance.

cross_activity_effects.A4: Configuration application selects active quorum; acknowledged application can trigger automatic leave.
cross_activity_effects.A7: Caller must apply through returned read index before serving a linearizable read.

after.execution_owner: Serialized raft instance; Node.run or caller-serialized RawNode
after.protocol_context: Local term, role, known leader and current voting configuration
after.trigger: Tick election timeout, Campaign/MsgHup, vote requests/replies, higher-term messages, same-term leader traffic, or CheckQuorum
implementation_guards: Campaign requires local voter progress, no in-progress snapshot and no committed unapplied configuration entries.
Vote grant requires eligible vote state and an up-to-date log. PreVote does not increment the local term; election does.
Candidate consumes only its current vote-response type; current joint voter sets decide quorum.
Term dispatch rejects old remote replies; higher terms generally reset authority, except PreVote and the check-quorum lease vote-request rule.
writes: Term and Vote; role/step/tick functions; lead; election and heartbeat elapsed; reset votes, readOnly tracker, replication progress and pendingConfIndex.
becomeLeader initializes self progress and appends a current-term empty entry, setting pendingConfIndex conservatively to the previous tail.
external_effects: Election request messages; durable-before-send vote responses including self-vote; initial leader append broadcast.
important_branches: CheckQuorum may relinquish leadership in the same term. PreCandidate resets votes without replacing term or vote.
reset does not erase committed log history; readOnly is replaced but pendingReadIndexMessages is a separate queue not cleared here.
Old MsgStorageAppendResp cannot stabilize entries but may acknowledge a committed snapshot; term-zero apply responses remain eligible across term changes.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Term and role filter qualify replication support; current-term empty entry enables advancement of retained older history.
cross_activity_effects.A6: Term/vote updates require persistence before affirmative support becomes usable.

after.protocol_context: Active AutoLeave joint configuration, current role, applied index and pendingConfIndex
after.trigger: Acknowledgment of applied entries or snapshot calls raft.appliedTo
implementation_guards: Requires AutoLeave, leader role and newApplied >= pendingConfIndex.
Uses zero-sized empty ConfChangeV2, avoiding proposal size refusal, but ordinary transfer rejection still applies.
writes: If accepted, proposal assigns pendingConfIndex and appends a leave-joint entry. Rejected transfer-time attempt records no separate retry flag.
important_branches: An eligible application acknowledgment tries once via Step(MsgProp); subsequent application acknowledgments can retry.
This only proposes exit; leaving the configuration still requires replication, commitment and application of the exit entry.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Exit proposal must commit using the current joint quorum before outgoing voters cease participating.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Leadership transfer suppresses the attempt; a newly elected leader appends an empty entry that can later drive application progress.

unknowns: After transfer rejects the last application-triggered attempt, is a future application acknowledgment guaranteed without new client proposals, or does abort leave no enabled retry?

after.execution_owner: Node/RawNode admission, leader readOnly tracker, and caller application
after.protocol_context: RequestCtx identity; leader term/configuration; committed read index
after.trigger: Propose/ReadIndex, first current-term commit, heartbeat context replies, ReadIndexResp
legal_preconditions: Caller correlates read results using RequestCtx and waits for application through index. Proposal/read request loss is permitted and retries are caller-owned.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased has clock and CheckQuorum assumptions; safe reads use voter confirmation.
external_effects: ReadStates or MsgReadIndexResp; proposal return only acknowledges submission, not commitment.
important_branches: Followers forward requests only with a known leader. Leaders postpone non-singleton reads before current-term commit.
Safe reads capture committed index and collect identity-matched heartbeat acknowledgments using current voter quorum; confirming a later queued context releases preceding requests.
reset replaces readOnly but not pendingReadIndexMessages; old pending requests must undergo current-term read processing before any result. Singleton has a direct committed-index response.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Safe-read authority consumes a quorum of context-correlated heartbeat responses separately from replication Match.

after.execution_owner: raft.applyConfChange and confchange.Changer, invoked by serialized caller
after.protocol_context: Active incoming/outgoing voter sets, learners, staged learners, AutoLeave and Progress
implementation_guards: Simple change modifies at most one voter and cannot empty incoming voters or run while joint.
Joint entry copies outgoing voters, applies changes to incoming, and preserves staged demotions until joint exit.
Leaving joint removes outgoing-only progress and clears AutoLeave; invariants enforce role/Progress compatibility.
writes: Replace Config and Progress, preserving retained peer progress through changer copies; update local learner status.
important_branches: Leader removal/demotion may step down if configured; otherwise removed leader stops accepting proposals.
Leader configuration changes recompute commitment and broadcast/probe; this path can advance committed but does not call releasePendingReadIndexMessages.
Abort transfer if transferee is no longer a voter. Configuration application itself does not call appliedTo.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Changes which stored Match values count toward majority/joint commitment.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Changes eligible voters and leader/transferee participation.

after.protocol_context: Current accepted leader term, local committed prefix and append predecessor identity
after.trigger: MsgApp or MsgHeartbeat after term/role dispatch
implementation_guards: Append predecessor index/term must match; conflicting committed entries cause panic instead of overwrite.
A request below committed is acknowledged at committed; normal appended Commit is capped at lastnewi.
Heartbeat uses the leader-provided Match-capped Commit; commitTo is monotonic and rejects beyond lastIndex.
writes: Replace conflicting uncommitted suffix; advance committed; update known leader and election elapsed through follower dispatch.
external_effects: Durable-before-send MsgAppResp with matched index or rejection hint; immediate heartbeat reply.

cross_activity_effects.A6: New log entries await persistence; app/vote support is held until durability.

after.protocol_context: Current leader term and active simple or joint voting sets
after.trigger: Client proposal, durable self-ack, peer MsgAppResp, heartbeat reply, or configuration recomputation
implementation_guards: Reject proposals during leadership transfer or when self has no Progress; enforce pending configuration checks and uncommitted size limit.
Leader response handling requires sender Progress after term dispatch. MaybeUpdate never lowers Match; quorum index uses voters only.
maybeCommit requires a strictly higher index with local log term equal to current leader term.
writes: Assign proposal term/index, append unstable log, enqueue durable self-ack.
Accepted append responses update Match, Next and flow control; quorum advancement changes committed.
external_effects: Append/heartbeat messages and retries; commit propagation; TimeoutNow when target catches up.

Rejection decreases probe position; heartbeat responses clear flow pause and prompt empty append when needed, including recovery from dropped inflights.

cross_activity_effects.A5: Committed watermark bounds entries handed to application.
cross_activity_effects.A7: Current-term commit permits pending safe-read processing.

after.protocol_context: Stable Storage overlaid by unstable entries and snapshot; outstanding Ready batches
after.trigger: Ready acceptance, Advance, MsgStorageAppendResp, initialization or term change
legal_preconditions: Caller persists required state before releasing dependent replies; async messages to each local worker are reliably processed in order.
RawNode is not thread-safe. Normal Ready must be handled then advanced; async mode uses supplied response messages instead of Advance.
writes: Track in-progress unstable entries; enqueue deferred self-support and storage completion; stableTo retires matching entries only.
durable_effects: Library schedules writes; actual disk IO and crash durability are caller duties. MemoryStorage is in-repository volatile storage, not a durable filesystem.
important_branches: Normal mode places remote deferred replies in Ready and self replies in stepsOnAdvance. Async mode attaches both to the ordered append work.

Append completion carries raft term as well as entry term/index; obsolete raft-term responses do not stabilize possibly overwritten history. A later hard-state write re-attests remaining unstable history in the new term.
Snapshot completion remains valid across terms because it represents committed state.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Delayed self and remote support prevents counting unpersisted entries.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Vote persistence and epoch-qualified completion protect authority/history transitions.
cross_activity_effects.A5: Async application exposes only locally stable committed entries.

after.protocol_context: Restarted state or snapshot with committed index, term and ConfState
implementation_guards: Obsolete snapshots at/below committed are ignored. Restoring requires follower and recipient membership; matching snapshot term/index fast-forwards commitment instead of replacing history.
Campaign is blocked until an outstanding snapshot completes. loadState bounds saved Commit within available history.
writes: Initialize log positions from storage and Config from saved ConfState; reset authority to follower. Actual snapshot replacement reconstructs config and unstable snapshot.
important_branches: Bootstrap explicitly creates initial committed membership entries and applies them internally, but caller still sees the entries for persistence/application.
Snapshot fast-forward retains existing configuration for subsequent ordinary entry application; full restoration replaces configuration.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Restores committed history and replication eligibility; uncommitted Match observations are rebuilt.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Snapshot/restart does not preserve active leader authority.
cross_activity_effects.A6: Snapshot data/config and retained entry term at compacted boundary reconstruct the log.

after.protocol_context: Same leader term with a tracked non-learner transferee
after.trigger: TransferLeader request; transferee append acknowledgment; tickHeartbeat election timeout; configuration removal of transferee
implementation_guards: Target must have Progress and not be a learner; self-target is ignored.
Proposals are dropped while leadTransferee is set. TimeoutNow is sent only when target Match equals local lastIndex.
writes: leadTransferee and electionElapsed; timeout/abort clears leadTransferee.
important_branches: Successful transfer causes a new election; unsuccessful transfer is aborted after electionTimeout ticks while still leader.
abortLeaderTransfer only clears the transferee; it does not call appliedTo or propose an entry.

cross_activity_effects.A4: The generic proposal rejection also covers the internally generated automatic leave-joint proposal.

after.meaning: The raft instance has recorded acknowledgment of application progress through applied. It is internal accounting; in normal mode the Node interface also permits early Advance before application finishes.
after.validity_context: Caller-ordered application/acknowledgment; term-independent committed work may acknowledge after authority changes.
after.durability: Not separately persisted by raft; caller supplies restart Applied and application state.
after.recovery: newRaft applies configured Applied to recovered log bounds.

after.meaning: The instance currently processes inputs in its selected role and term; a leader role results from quorum election support. This is local authority state, not proof of an unexpired external lease.
after.validity_context: Configured voters and serialized term dispatch; same-term role loss remains possible.
after.durability: Term and Vote are emitted for persistence; role and leader are volatile.
after.recovery: Restart loads term/vote then becomes follower.

after.meaning: The local committed watermark identifies an immutable accepted prefix eligible for ordered application, subject to local stability and snapshot handling. It does not assert application completed.

identity.prefix: Committed log index and associated log history

after.validity_context: Monotonic within the instance; leader quorum/current-term advancement, follower accepted leader propagation, or committed snapshot/recovery.
after.durability: HardState and log/snapshot are written by caller according to Ready contract.
after.recovery: Load saved Commit and snapshot boundary; reject inconsistent bounds.

after.meaning: The active configuration records incoming and optional outgoing voters, learner roles and whether the joint state requests automatic exit. AutoLeave records policy, not an already-enqueued exit proposal or completed transition.

identity.configuration: Applied ConfChange sequence or restored ConfState

after.validity_context: From committed configuration application or initialization/restoration until the next configuration update. Quorum formation uses both sets while outgoing voters remain.
after.durability: Configuration is represented in committed history and recorded ConfState snapshots by the caller.
after.recovery: confchange.Restore rebuilds sets and AutoLeave from ConfState; Bootstrap establishes initial peers.

after.meaning: Within leader tracking, peer Match is the highest acknowledged matching prefix known for that peer. Self Match is initialized at reset to local tail and later updated by durable self-ack; the current-term commitment check prevents that initialization alone committing an older tail.

identity.leader: Local node ID and leader term

after.validity_context: Current leader epoch and peer Progress membership; not a heartbeat or client completion fact.
after.durability: Volatile evidence; remote support assumes durable response contract.
after.recovery: Reset rebuilds peer progress rather than loading prior Match.

formation.explanation: A leader assigns term/index to proposals, emits log appends and defers its self-ack until persistence. Followers check predecessor identity, preserve committed entries, append the uncommitted suffix and return durability-dependent support. In the leader term, known-peer positive replies update Match; voting majority (both halves if joint) yields a candidate index, and matching the current term permits committed advancement. Broadcast append and Match-capped heartbeat propagate the decision. Ready then exposes the ordered committed prefix subject to snapshot and local-stability/application-size constraints; caller application and acknowledgment consume it. Rejection hints, heartbeat-driven empty appends and snapshot fallback support recovery without treating activity as matched history.

context.explanation: Election starts only from a promotable instance with no committed unapplied configuration. PreVote probes without raising term; real campaign increments term and counts persisted self/peer votes using current voter sets and log freshness. Higher-term dispatch or loss of quorum can relinquish authority; same-term leader traffic demotes candidates. Reset clears transient vote/read/peer-progress state but retains log and committed decisions. Older network replies are rejected; append-storage completions are term-qualified, whereas committed snapshot/apply completions survive term changes. Leadership transfer first catches up a tracked voter, then sends TimeoutNow and suppresses proposals until takeover or timeout.

connection.explanation: A2 qualifies whose A1 support can be consumed: term dispatch and reset prevent a new leader from aggregating old-term replication replies, and the current-term entry requirement ties retained older log history to fresh quorum support. Committed decisions are term-independent, so application/storage snapshot acknowledgment may complete after leadership changes; overwritable append history instead needs a current-term durability attestation. Applied configuration changes alter the voter sets used by both election and replication quorums, while campaign blocks unapplied committed membership. Automatic joint exit is a separate application-triggered proposal, so recorded AutoLeave and recorded application do not themselves mean exit was scheduled. Pending read-only acknowledgments reset with authority; the pre-current-term request queue survives reset and is reprocessed through current-term read logic on an append-response commit.

open_details: Whether automatic leave can lose its continuation when transfer suppresses the final application-triggered attempt and later times out.
Whether configuration-triggered commitment can be the first current-term commit with pending reads, despite campaign restrictions.
Early-Advance configuration ordering, detailed membership/removal read interactions, and broader concurrent snapshot/apply histories remain uninvestigated variants.
after.rationale: Representative formation and authority paths were traced through producers, quorum aggregation, persistence, dispatch, configuration, recovery and application. This is a navigable initial explanation, not full path coverage or defect evidence.

after.reason: Node interface permits early Advance; ordering relative to configuration application and automatic exit needs separate contract investigation. The selected transfer question will apply configuration before Advance.
Library boundary explicitly delegates IO and application; only sourced caller contracts, not a deployment implementation, are available.
Specific unresolved continuation premise: a heartbeat-only Advance does not acknowledge applied entries, so the comment promising retry on next advance needs a legal-history discriminator.

Unlike append-response commitment this path does not release pending reads. Whether it can establish the first current-term commit with pending reads is unresolved; campaign forbids committed unapplied config, which is concrete counterevidence. Read request loss is expressly permitted.
InteractionEnv wraps RawNode nodes, messages and test handlers. Detailed storage/transport handlers remain unread; no helper legality or scheduling guarantees are assumed.

after.system_boundary: Captured go.etcd.io/raft/v3 library: serialized raft state machine, Node/RawNode wrappers, quorum/configuration tracking, log/unstable and MemoryStorage. Production network, durable disk and business application are caller-owned; in-repository implementations are included where read.

Caller owns transport, durable writes, ordered application, periodic Tick, and retries.
